top3.headline: Apple cuts staff AI budgets while pushing employees to use more AI
top3.whyItMatters: If Apple caps AI spend per person, your teams will need clear budgets for agent use.

top3.headline: Claude Code subagent status updates now cost about 99% less
top3.whyItMatters: Cheaper background agents mean more work per seat before teams hit usage limits.

top3.headline: OpenAI will acquire Pierre to build Git workflows for coding agents
top3.whyItMatters: Reviewing agent-written code is now a platform contest, and OpenAI wants to own that workflow.

items.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 adds animated GIFs and reference images
items.takeaway: OpenAI says two new image models are coming to the API with 50% faster generation.
items.soWhat: Teams can now make simple animations inside ChatGPT without a separate design tool.

items.title: OpenAI's autonomous pipeline generated patches for 948 Linux kernel flaws
items.takeaway: One run with an unreleased cyber model cost $1.2 million in API fees; upstream status not stated.
items.soWhat: Bug discovery is scaling with AI, so budget for faster patching across your own stack.

items.title: Perplexity's Decisions API can now ground answers in the live web
items.takeaway: Setting mode to web_grounding runs one Fast Search query per question, at $0.001 per search.
items.soWhat: Automated batch decisions can now use current facts for a fraction of a cent each.

items.title: Researcher finds 73 fake AI agent tool repos spreading malware
items.takeaway: They posed as Claude skills, Codex and MCP servers; 51 were still live. Single report.
items.soWhat: Install skills and MCP servers only from vetted sources, since fake ones are spreading.

items.title: Anthropic used Claude to map a vault particle's structure in days
items.takeaway: Manual work would have taken weeks to months; researchers had to fix some simple mistakes.
items.soWhat: AI is shortening lab research timelines, but experts still need to check its work.

items.title: Apple cuts staff AI budgets while pushing employees to use more AI
items.takeaway: Engineers' daily limit fell from $300 to $200, with $100 planned; some teams could drop to $25.
items.soWhat: Per-person AI spending caps are arriving, so decide now how you will budget agent use.

items.title: Claude Code subagent status updates now cost about 99% less
items.takeaway: Haiku 5.5 now writes the 30-second status line from short notes instead of rereading the conversation.
items.soWhat: Background agents are getting cheaper to run, which stretches every team's usage limits.

items.title: Nous Research puts Hermes Agent plugins and skills in one marketplace
items.takeaway: A 7-day plugin hackathon offers $20,000 in cash prizes.
items.soWhat: Agent platforms now compete on extensions, so favor ones with a vetted plugin catalog.

items.title: Ripple-65B claims the top US open-weight score for agentic coding
items.takeaway: Self-reported 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1 at a stated $32M full R&D cost; Benaich notes China still leads.
items.soWhat: Smaller open models that run locally keep closing in, lowering the cost of in-house agents.

items.title: Texas, the fastest-growing data center market, may slow AI buildouts
items.takeaway: The governor-elect backed a moratorium; Nexus Hubbard, mostly for Anthropic, is planned at 6,400 MW.
items.soWhat: Plan for compute delays, since even Texas may halt new data center projects.

items.title: Coding-agent app Conductor joins Meta Superintelligence Labs
items.takeaway: Charlie Holtz says the team will work on 'the next interface' with Nat Friedman and Alexandr Wang; terms undisclosed.
items.soWhat: Big labs are absorbing coding-agent teams, so expect fewer independent tools to choose from.

items.title: OpenAI will acquire Pierre to build Git workflows for coding agents
items.takeaway: Pierre's libraries already power the Codex app; its open-source projects stay open; closing needs approval.
items.soWhat: Reviewing agent-written code is becoming a core platform, not a side tool.

hotOnX.text: Claude helped map the first 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle; preprint submitted to bioRxiv.
hotOnX.note: A concrete case of AI speeding up real lab science, with its mistakes disclosed.

hotOnX.text: Apple is cutting employee AI budgets: engineers' daily limits went from $300 to $200.
hotOnX.note: Even the richest companies are now rationing AI spend per employee.

hotOnX.text: Autonomous pipeline validated and generated patches for 948 Linux kernel privilege escalation bugs in one run.
hotOnX.note: AI finding kernel bugs at this scale changes the economics of security work.
